title: A Critical and Exegetical Commentary on Haggai, Zechariah, Malachi and Jonah (International Critical Commentary)

verification_log.method: pp. 20–22: Darius's first full year from Nisan 521; Haggai's first date (1/VI of year 2) "about the middle of August" 520, the work beginning days later; the movement came when the eastern revolts against Darius suggested the empire's collapse; 24/IX = December 520, the height of enthusiasm; pp. 62–63: 2:7 means the nations' "precious things" coming to the temple; the older Messianic reading (Vulgate desideratus, with Luke 2) "is now generally abandoned"; pp. 76–78: 2:23 — Haggai "identified Zerubbabel with the long-expected son of David"; the signet as one's most precious possession

access_notes: Read through the Internet Archive OCR text. Haggai and Zechariah 1–8 are by H. G. Mitchell.
